summary: The AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator returns mdl points. The inputs are the hand Release Push-Ups (HRP) in 2 minutes, the sprint-Drag-Carry (SDC) time, the plank (PLK) time and the two-Mile Run (2MR) time. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator work?
sections.html:
The AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports mdl points in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the age group, the AFT standard and the sex); then you type in the hand Release Push-Ups (HRP) in 2 minutes, the sprint-Drag-Carry (SDC) time, the plank (PLK) time and the two-Mile Run (2MR) time.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: The formula behind the AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Mdl points=(1, age group, AFT standard, sex, 3-Rep Max Deadlift (MDL))
Hrp points=(2, age group, AFT standard, sex, hand Release Push-Ups (HRP) in 2 minutes)
Sdc points=(3, age group, AFT standard, sex, sprint-Drag-Carry (SDC) time)
Plk points=(4, age group, AFT standard, sex, plank (PLK) time)
Tmr points=(5, age group, AFT standard, sex, two-Mile Run (2MR) time)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Mass, opening in pounds
  • Time, opening in minutes / seconds

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the hand Release Push-Ups (HRP) in 2 minutes, the sprint-Drag-Carry (SDC) time and the plank (PLK) time — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns mdl points, derived from the hand Release Push-Ups (HRP) in 2 minutes, the sprint-Drag-Carry (SDC) time and the plank (PLK) time. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the hand Release Push-Ups (HRP) in 2 minutes, the sprint-Drag-Carry (SDC) time, the plank (PLK) time and the two-Mile Run (2MR) time, which is 14 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter 3-Rep Max Deadlift (MDL) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. 3-Rep Max Deadlift (MDL) opens in pounds and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (8 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the AFT (US Army Fitness Test) calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
